name: Zig
summary: A systems language and toolchain that makes allocation explicit at API boundaries, evaluates selected code at comptime, and integrates cross-target builds and C interoperability.

features.name: Explicit allocator boundary
features.description: Zig's language reference presents allocation as an explicit operation selected by the program: code can accept an allocator, allocate through it, and release resources according to the allocator's contract. The language does not impose one global heap allocator on all code.
benefits: Makes allocation strategy and lifetime responsibility visible at API boundaries
Allows programs to select allocators appropriate to their environment
costs: Callers and callees must agree on allocator ownership and deallocation
Incorrect lifetime or allocator pairing remains a program-level failure mode

features.name: Comptime evaluation and specialization
features.description: Zig supports comptime-known variables and expressions whose loads, stores, and control flow are evaluated during semantic analysis. The reference also describes generic data structures built with compile-time parameters and reflection.
benefits: Moves selected computation and specialization before runtime
Provides generic and reflective abstractions without requiring a separate macro language
costs: Compile-time execution increases compiler work and can expose compile-time resource limits
The boundary between generated behavior and runtime behavior must remain understandable

features.name: Typed error and optional values
features.description: Zig represents recoverable failure with error sets and error-union types, and represents absence with optional types. The reference defines operators and control-flow forms for propagating or handling these values.
benefits: Keeps common failure and absence cases in function and value types
Makes propagation and handling points explicit in source
costs: Callers must account for additional union cases at use sites
Error-set composition and optional unwrapping add type-checking and API design surface

features.name: Cross-target build and C integration
features.description: The Zig reference documents a build system with target selection, build modes, WebAssembly targets, and C import/export facilities. These features make target and foreign-ABI choices part of the toolchain surface.
benefits: Provides one toolchain surface for multiple target environments
Supports incremental adoption through C headers and ABI-compatible exports
costs: Target, linker, ABI, and platform configuration expand build complexity
C interoperability inherits the correctness and lifetime assumptions of the foreign interface

mathematical_views.question: How do allocator selection, allocation, ownership transfer, and deallocation constrain a Zig program's memory transitions?
assumptions: Allocated regions and allocator instances are vertices with explicit ownership or borrowing edges
A deallocation transition is valid only when the responsible allocator and lifetime contract permit it
The view abstracts allocator implementation details and platform-specific virtual memory

mathematical_views.question: Which parts of a Zig program are resolved during comptime, and which remain runtime transitions?
assumptions: Comptime evaluation is modeled as a preprocessing or specialization transition over typed values and declarations
Runtime execution begins only for values and control flow not resolved by the selected comptime context
The view does not claim that every optimization or generated instruction is determined by comptime

mathematical_views.question: How might target, build-mode, and foreign-ABI choices alter the set of compilation and linking actions?
assumptions: Build options and target descriptors are graph inputs, and compilation or linking actions are dependent vertices
The graph is a candidate analysis of documented toolchain structure rather than a complete build trace
Platform-specific behavior and package-manager policy are outside the view

costs: Ownership and allocator compatibility become API obligations
More compile-time work and a larger semantic boundary
Additional union cases must be handled by callers

benefits: Integrated target and foreign-language toolchain support
costs: Target and ABI configuration increase build complexity
